title: School or early learning lockdown
version: Ministry of Education 'Planning and preparing for emergencies: Practical information and guidance for schools and early childhood services' (October 2026, ISBN 978-1-75991-452-7); Ministry of Education 'Prepare for an emergency or traumatic incident' pages for schools (updated 17 Sep 2026) and early learning (updated 19 Oct 2026); Ministry of Education parents page 'Emergency events' (updated 4 May 2026); Ministry of Education 'Respond at school to an emergency or traumatic incident' (updated 21 Sep 2026); NZ Police 'Know what to do: Escape. Hide. Tell' (no date, copyright 2026); SUPERSEDED earlier edition 'Planning and preparing for emergencies' (January 2025) for wording differences only; all read 21 Nov 2026
sourceNote: Direct download refused (proxy blocks education.govt.nz, web-assets.education.govt.nz and police.govt.nz), so every line was read by a fetch tool asked to quote exact lines in short pieces (rejoined). No PDF was in sources/. All sources are NZ; no Australian source used. Sections: A Ministry guide October 2026 (main): A1 basic emergency response process (call 111, or 105 if not urgent); A2 communicating (staff channel, student phones may alert an intruder, parent message template 'URGENT: The centre/school is currently in lockdown due to [reason]... Do not come to the centre until advised', and 'The emergency has ended' template); A3 alarms and signals (distinct signals; for an intruder it may not be appropriate to sound any alarm; how to signal the end; automatic bells); A4 shelter in place vs lockdown (lockdown = threat directly related to the school/centre, e.g. attacker on grounds; shelter in place = external threat), who can initiate, lock/secure doors, bathroom only if safe and accompanied by an adult, lock down if information is limited, step down to shelter in place, who lifts it (whoever initiated; Police advise when they initiated), lockdown kit; A5 Escape. Hide. Tell. (hide: silence phone, lock doors and windows, barricade, stay away from doors, quiet and still; tell: 111 when safe); A6 drills (schools with students present; early childhood lockdown drills without children; ECE drills at least once every 4 months); A7 debriefing; A8 reuniting (up to 10 pre-authorised people); A9 example procedure checklist p45 (receive instruction, initiate e.g. 'sounding airhorn 3 times' as a fill-in example, check everyone inside and note anyone unaccounted for, secure, notify Police, staff channel, off-site groups, parents stay away, Ministry local office, toilets/first aid/food, advised to move to shelter in place, advised to come out, reunification or resume usual activities); A10 Appendix 1 respond and recovery (Traumatic incident team 0800 848 326). B Ministry web pages (threat by email/post/phone: call NZ Police, who may advise lockdown; 111 emergency, 105 non-emergency). C parents page (stay away until officially told it is safe; if your child contacts you, be calm). D respond page (111; TI team 0800 848 326, any time). E NZ Police Escape Hide Tell page (what to tell 111: location, offender description and direction, weapons, number of people and injured, intent; stay on the line; do not move closer). F SUPERSEDED January 2025 edition (lockdown: move to closest classrooms and lock doors immediately, take attendance if possible with a list of missing and extra children, remain in room until Police instruct or a formal announcement ends it, bathroom if permitted and accompanied by a designated staff member, camp toilets; Police usually say lockdown rather than shelter in place; 1.23 checklist; children not in drills for violent situations). Not captured: the school and early learning emergency management plan templates (DOCX could not be read, so any school-specific lockdown signal, roles or all-clear wording in them is missing); Appendix 1 deter/detect/delay and resilience text; heading of the 'emergency has ended' message template; whether the October 2026 Appendix 1 still says children should not be in drills for violent situations. Differences: roll check is 'take attendance, if possible, and prepare a list of missing and extra children' (F, 2025) vs 'Check that everyone is inside. Note any names of anyone who is unaccounted for.' (A9, 2026); bathroom accompanied by 'a designated staff member' (F) vs 'an adult' (A4); 'until the further notice' (A4) vs 'until further instruction is received from NZ Police or until a formal announcement is made' (F); Escape wording longer in A5 and E than in A10; F said children/young people should not be in violent-situation drills while A6 and F3 say school lockdown drills should be practised with students present (ECE: without children). Gaps: no Ministry or Police source found says to close blinds/curtains or turn lights off (Police says lock doors and windows, barricade, stay away from doors, be quiet and still); no fixed alert signal (left to each school's plan; airhorn 3 times is only a fill-in example); no fixed all-clear signal or wording (each plan decides 'How will you signal the end'); nothing on children found outside or in toilets when the alert sounds, beyond 'everyone moves to... the required location' and moving to the closest rooms (F); no rule on whether to open a locked door to someone knocking (only stay until lifted); no times or durations for a lockdown; no formal incident-reporting form or deadline (only debrief, Ministry local office, TI team).
status: Reviewer: 5 instructions missed and 15 findings, all fixed (2 partly); no national alert signal or durations. 166 of 166 quotes exact (web copy).
